title: Derived sections and total limit with specified projections
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ be the morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose inverse image on underlying sheaves is the constant sequence, and whose ring map is given by $A\to B_n$. Let $U$ be exact termwise scalar restriction and $G=R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}\circ U$ be the strict-system derived sections functor with its finite comparison of [lem-coef-sequence-global-sections-evaluation]. Write $Rp_*$ and $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ for the total derived direct images computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ for total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For $J\in D(\mathscr S(B))$ there is a specified isomorphism, natural in $J$, $$R\Gamma(\mathcal C,Rp_*J)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\,G(J).$$ The comparison retains the actual finite projections: its nth projection is global sections of the total-limit projection followed by the scalar-restriction comparison at level $n$. All resolutions and comparisons are in the strict derived system categories, rather than unrelated choices at the fibers.

proof.text: Use the existing coefficient-universe Grothendieck theorems for module sheaves and strict systems. The countable tower category is Grothendieck: take evaluation-left-adjoint images of a separator, use componentwise filtered colimits, and use componentwise locally small hom sets. K-injective localization therefore supplies the universal inverse-limit pairs LA and LB.

Apply the inverse-limit acyclicity clause of the normalized sequence-projection theorem. Its restriction U0 is naturally isomorphic to the specified restriction U: the level isomorphisms identify both with actual scalar restriction, and the stated sectionwise transition equations prove tower naturality. Resolve UI by a K-injective K and precompose its resolution with this isomorphism. The cited clause makes lim(UI) to lim(K) a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the LA unit then makes its value on UI invertible. Hence U on derived categories followed by LA is a universal derived pair P for the actual projection direct image.

For constant coefficients, lim preserves K-injectives by its exact constant-sequence left adjoint. Thus LA followed by derived sections is a universal derived pair for lim followed by ordinary sections. For the other order, resolve a K-injective tower I by a tower J with injective terms; the resolution is a homotopy equivalence. Injective towers have split successor transitions, and any additive functor preserves these splittings. The split-transition kernel/Roos short exact sequence and exact products in abelian groups make the ordinary-limit-to-Roos comparison a quasi-isomorphism for termwise sections of J. The normalized exact-products Roos theorem identifies its localization with the LB unit. Naturality and the homotopy equivalence give invertibility on termwise sections of I. This makes derived termwise sections followed by LB the second universal derived pair.

Global sections preserve ordinary tower limits. Localize the canonical preservesLimitNatIso, whose nth projection is sections of the ordinary cone projection. Uniqueness of total right derived functors gives the constant-coefficient comparison, normalized by the two composite units. Whisker it with exact derived restriction to obtain kappa for strict systems. Its naturality against the exact-functor factorization gives the asserted equation on every complex.

Derive the natural ordinary projections lim to evaluation by the universal property of LA and LB; their factorization equations give the two unit/projection identities. For the constant comparison, check the projection identity on K-injective representatives, canceling the invertible composite unit. Use the comparison normalization, the ordinary preservesLimitNatIso projection equation, and the given normalized sections/evaluation equation. Tower evaluation is K-injective, so its finite unit can be canceled. Natural isomorphisms to K-injective representatives extend the identity to every derived object. Finally whisker by exact restriction and compose with the given derived restriction/evaluation and scalar isomorphisms. Expanding finiteEvaluation gives precisely the last displayed equality.
